instruction: Extract the 7 principles for writing effective prompts from the PowerPoint presentation 'Unlocking-the-Power-of-ChatGPT.pptx' (found on the 'Principles' slide) and save them as a bulleted list in a new Writer document named 'principles.docx' on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

items: One Prompt, One Idea, One Conversation
Use complete sentences and avoid jargon or complex language

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the 7 principles from slide 20 ('Principles' slide) of the PowerPoint. Verified by reading the PowerPoint: slide 20 contains exactly 7 principles listed. The evaluator checks both the count (7 items) and the content of each principle (50% score for count, 50% for content match).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 50% for correct count (7 principles), 50% for having all expected principles in the document

Getter logic doesn't check paragraph style/format (e.g., list_style from python-docx) to verify bullets are used.
Header filtering is fragile - only excludes 'Principles' and 'ChatGPT Principles', but other text in document would be counted as principles.
Positive: Content matching uses exact string comparison which is appropriate for this task.
Positive: Scoring breakdown (50% count, 50% content) is reasonable.
Positive: Postconfig appropriately saves the document before verification.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Update getter to check paragraph bullet formatting using python-docx's paragraph.style or checking if paragraph has list numbering/bullets.
Add logic to verify paragraphs are actually formatted as list items, not just plain text.
Consider more robust header filtering or better document structure validation.
